messages:
alex: Heads-up — sketching a rewrap/rotation runbook for Key Vaults used as KEKs across tenants. Want feedback on cross-tenant auth, MI choices, audit hooks, and scale concerns.

maria: +1. High-level: prefer user-assigned MI tied to the VM/AKS identity, RBAC-enabled vaults, use wrap/unwrap for DEKs, keep key versions alive until rewrap completes.

samir: Quick Q: are we planning to rotate by creating a new key (new key resource) vs new key version? Pros/cons?

leah: From ops: new key version = same key resource id, easier to keep access permissions intact. New key resource lets you do a cleaner separation and different key types. For HSM-backed we might prefer separate keys if algorithm differs.

alex: Agreed. Proposed runbook (concise):
1) Create new KEK (v2) in Vault (either new version or new key)
2) Update provisioning so new writes use KEK v2 for wrapKey
3) Start async rewrap job: for each object, unwrap wrappedDEK with v1 -> wrap with v2 -> update record
4) Keep v1 available for unwrapping until checkpoint shows 100% migrated + buffer window
5) Soft-delete only after archive period + confirm audit

maria: Important: enable purge protection on vaults if regulatory. Also configure soft-delete retention in minutes/days per policy.

samir: Audit logging: send KeyVaultDiagnostics to Log Analytics + Event Hub -> SIEM. Track operations: WrapKey, UnwrapKey, Encrypt, Decrypt, Get, Sign, Verify. Alert on abnormal UnwrapKey spikes or unwraps by unexpected principal.

leah: Tenant boundary stuff — reminder: system-assigned MI cannot cross tenants. Only option for cross-tenant access is: create SP in vault tenant and exchange creds or invite SP as guest, both messy. Realistically for multi-tenant customers we should host compute in same tenant or run per-tenant Private deployment.

alex: Documenting a cross-tenant pattern we tried: create a service principal (app registration) in vault tenant, give it Key Vault RBAC role, then create short-lived cert/secret and rotate. But operationally complex and audit surface increases.

maria: RBAC vs access policies: new guidance — default to RBAC for vaults created after 2021. Access Policies are legacy; if migration needed, script mapping of key/secret/certificate permissions to RBAC roles. Test thoroughly.

samir: Code sample for wrap using az identity token + curl (for debugging):
```
# get token for vault resource
TOKEN=$(az account get-access-token --resource https://vault.azure.net --query accessToken -o tsv)
curl -X POST "https://{vault}.vault.azure.net/keys/{key-name}/wrapKey?api-version=7.2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"alg":"RSA-OAEP","value":"BASE64_DEK"}'
```
Use SDK in prod; this is only for repro.

leah: Rewrap at scale: watch for 429s and throttling. Our suggestion: shard by prefix, use a distributed checkpoint (Cosmos/DB) to track progress, exponential backoff with jitter, and a concurrency cap per vault to avoid throttling.

alex: Also add a safety pattern: when rewrapping, write new wrappedDEK and keep old wrappedDEK until object confirms successful decrypt with v2; perform atomic update then garbage collect old wrap after retention window.

maria: Role lists (least-privilege): assign built-in role "Key Vault Crypto User" to MIs for wrap/unwrap. If you want finer scope, assign action rights: Microsoft.KeyVault/keys/wrap/action, Microsoft.KeyVault/keys/unwrap/action, and Microsoft.KeyVault/keys/get/action.

samir: Encryption algorithm selection: RSA-OAEP for RSA keys, A256KW for symmetric keys (Managed HSM supports AES-KW). Detect key.kty and pick accordingly. HSM-backed keys have stronger attestation lines.

leah: Ops runbook checks before rotation: vault diagnostics ON, private endpoint pinned, RBAC enabled, MI is user-assigned, soft-delete on, purge-protection configured if needed. infra-bot: please verify.

infra-bot: deploy-check: keyvault_diagnostics=true; private_endpoint=true; rbac_enabled=true; mi_type=user_assigned; soft_delete_days=90; purge_protection=true

alex: Threat model note: consider an attacker with access to wrappedDEKs storage but not vault — wrapping keeps DEKs safe. If attacker compromises MI credentials, track suspicious UnwrapKey ops and consider immediate rotation + revoke MI credentials.

maria: Recovery/rollback: keep old KEK versions for rollback; ensure backup/export procedures for keys follow compliance (HSM keys often can't be exported). Document manual rewrap steps in case automation fails.

samir: One more operational tip: for dev/test vaults we allow access policies for faster setup, but never use them in prod. Put an automated test that validates wrap/unwrap roundtrip during CI.

leah: I'll draft the pipeline design: sharded rewrap workers, checkpoint store, throttling controls, telemetry on unwrap/wrap counts, error queue for manual review.

alex: Perfect. I'll turn this into an RFC and a short playbook (runbook + CLI snippets + alert rules) and link it into the Private deployment onboarding checklist. Tagging @maria @samir for reviews.
